paper.subject: astronomy
paper.title: IOAA´s 2012 2nd try Observational Exam
paper.organiser: By Fernando Vieira and Marcos Mataratzis
paper.caveat: Star charts 4–6 are supplied from the corresponding Bulgarian observational packet. Its filename is English, but its task sheet and captions are Bulgarian. The original English text-only edition and its inline key are retained: task2 gives only a)1.5 and b)0.5 without explaining these values; no missing drawing is invented. The time limits differ between the English and Bulgarian packets, so the English inline key governs this edition.

transcription.verifiedBy: mechanical:single-pass-gates (single-pass source transcription; automated schema, math and crop-evidence checks; no separate model checker, prompt v2)
transcription.notes: Single-pass Astra read all2 original English text/key pages plus all4 Bulgarian companion pages; exact page hashes bound in reading checkpoint. Existing transcription used only as draft and checked against those originals. Restored two printed misspellings separeted/Identiffy; original English inline key timings retained. Three missing star charts recovered from companion DOCX; original Bulgarian edition already canonical, so no duplicate added. No separate model checker.

problems.statement: Use your green laser pointer to aim at 3 zodiacal constellations of your choice. (2 min)

solution.statement: Student will have **2 minutes** to accomplish this task.

problems.statement:
Point to $\nu$ Scorpii (***star chart-4***). If you are not able to point at the star you can ask the instructor to do it for you but you will not get points for this. (3 min)

Use 2x barlow + 10mm eyepiece to draw what you see through the eyepiece. You don´t need to mark North . (2 min)

[[figure p2-fig1]]

figures.caption: Star chart 4 — Scorpius. From the original Bulgarian companion packet.

problems.statement:
Point your telescope to the star SAO 209318 (***star chart-5***). Notice a small nebulous patch close to that star. Use your 10mm or 10mm + 2x barlow to estimate the distance between the star and the nebulous patch, in arc minutes. (coordinates to SAO 209318 are $\alpha$: 17h50m51s and $\delta$: -37°02’). Express your answer using 0.5’ precision knowing that the field of view of the 10mm eyepiece on this telescope is 24 arcmin or 0.4º. If you are not able to point at the star, the instructor will do it for you but you lose 50% of the points. (2 min pointing, 3 min determining the distance)

[[figure p3-fig1]]

figures.caption: Star chart 5 — Scorpius. From the original Bulgarian companion packet.

answer.note: Official key: ~ 4.5’ (4’18”); 4 to 5 arc minutes count as 100% correct, 3.0 – 3.9 or 5.1 – 6.0 arc minutes as 70% correct.

solution.statement: R: **~ 4.5’** (4’18”). 4 to 5 arc minutes will be considered 100% correct answers. 3.0 – 3.9 or 5.1 – 6.0 arc minutes will be considered 70% correct. **(5 minutes)**
